document: Mandate for Leadership: The Conservative Promise (Project 2025, Heritage Foundation, April 2023; editors Paul Dans and Steven Groves; foreword Kevin D. Roberts; closing essay 'Onward!' by Edwin J. Feulner)
pdf_note: static.project2025.org now redirects (302) to https://www.mandateforleadership.org/ (observed 2026-11-08). The congress.gov copy given by the user (https://www.congress.gov/118/meeting/house/117694/documents/HHRG-118-GO05-20240925-SD004.pdf) could not be fetched; its identity is inferred from the hearing record (see 'hearing').

chapters.title: White House Office
proposals: Fill the government with more political appointees, on the premise that the first Trump administration appointed too few
Remove personnel judged not loyal to the conservative agenda
Select a White House Counsel 'deeply committed' to the president's 'America First' agenda (Wikipedia's summary)
Reconsider accommodations for the White House press corps (Wikipedia's summary)

chapters.title: Executive Office of the President of the United States
chapters.agency: EOP / OMB / NSC / CEA / OSTP / CEQ
proposals: OMB to use 'every possible tool' to impose fiscal discipline; president to make 'aggressive use' of power 'to bend or break the bureaucracy to the presidential will'
Reinstate political appointees (Program Associate Directors) signing apportionments; appoint an OMB General Counsel willing to challenge precedent
Use federal procurement (OFPP) to push back on 'woke' corporate policies
NSC to eliminate directorates not aligned with the president's agenda; fill national-security roles with politically vetted officials
CEQ to eliminate the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Carbon; OSTP to reshape the US Global Change Research Program
Revoke EO 14020 (Gender Policy Council); appoint a Special Assistant for 'life and family' issues
Bring independent agencies under direct presidential control (Wikipedia's summary)

chapters.title: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
proposals: Reinstate Schedule F to reclassify tens of thousands of 'policy-influencing' civil servants as at-will
Reinstate Trump-era EOs 13836, 13837 and 13839 curbing federal unions and speeding discipline
Reduce the roughly 2.95 million-person federal workforce
Use the Plum Book and a vetted personnel database/questionnaire to staff political positions
Require federal contractors' workforces to be 70% US citizens, rising to 95% (Wikipedia's summary)

chapters.title: Department of Defense
proposals: Expand and modernize the nuclear arsenal: LGM-35 Sentinel, W87-1, W88 Alt 370, SLCM-N, multiple warheads on Minuteman III, nuclear-armed hypersonic systems; move NNSA to 'a wartime footing'; be willing to test despite the CTBT
Extend the US nuclear umbrella only to NATO members and raise expectations of allies such as Japan and South Korea
Abolish DEI programs in the Department and reinstate service members discharged over COVID-19 vaccination
Bar consideration of climate change in national-security threat assessments
Treat China as the principal threat to be countered

chapters.title: Department of Homeland Security
proposals: Pursue legislation to abolish DHS and create a Cabinet-level border and immigration agency combining CBP, ICE, USCIS, HHS's ORR and DOJ's EOIR/OIL
Fund 100,000 detention beds (allowing tents), 20,000 ERO officers; apply expedited removal nationwide; rescind 'sensitive zone' limits on arrests at schools, hospitals and churches
Restore Remain in Mexico and Title 42; repeal TVPRA Section 235 protections for unaccompanied children; end the Flores settlement; eliminate T and U visas; make E-Verify mandatory

Shift FEMA disaster costs to states (federal share from 25% for small disasters, capped at 75%); replace the National Flood Insurance Program with private insurance; condition FEMA grants on immigration cooperation
Privatize TSA screening; narrow CISA to cybersecurity and end its counter-misinformation work; eliminate DHS's Office of Intelligence and Analysis

chapters.title: Department of State
proposals: Dismiss State Department leadership before January 20, 2025 and fill roles with acting appointees not requiring Senate confirmation
Favor transactional bilateral deals over maintaining alliances; refocus Africa policy on countering China
Eliminate or sharply reduce visas for students from 'enemy nations'
Skip congressional approval for some foreign arms sales (Wikipedia's summary)

Related objectives tracked by project2025.observer: withdraw from WHO and UN Human Rights Council, defund UNRWA, reinstate the Mexico City policy, curtail refugee admissions, bar rainbow flags at embassies

chapters.title: Intelligence Community
proposals: Chapter-level proposals could not be independently verified in this session beyond the document's framing of China and other communist states as the principal national-security threat (Wikipedia). Carmack was John Ratcliffe's chief of staff at ODNI; Ratcliffe is credited as a contributor (AP via Fortune, Wikipedia list).

chapters.title: Media Agencies
authors: Mora Namdar (U.S. Agency for Global Media)
proposals: Defund the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (NPR and PBS)
Consider revoking NPR stations' noncommercial status and moving them off the 88-92 FM band (Wikipedia's summary)
Overhaul Voice of America/USAGM so it serves presidential foreign-policy messaging (critics' characterization: 'arm of the Oval Office')

chapters.title: Agency for International Development
proposals: Remove the words 'gender,' 'abortion,' 'reproductive health' and 'sexual and reproductive rights' from all USAID programs and documents
'Dismantle USAID's DEI apparatus' (chapter wording per OnTheIssues excerpt)
End USAID climate programming and campaigns against 'systemic racism'; reconsider promotion of abortion as health care
Reorient aid toward countering China

chapters.title: Department of Agriculture
proposals: Tighten SNAP work requirements and reduce eligibility; separate nutrition programs from the farm bill
Reduce school-meal eligibility (Community Eligibility Provision) and eliminate summer meals
Cut crop-insurance subsidy rates; eliminate the Conservation Reserve Program; drop wetland/erodible-land conservation compliance
Remove climate change and equity from the department's mission; repeal the federal Dietary Guidelines
Increase timber sales; rescind the Roadless Rule for the Tongass National Forest

chapters.title: Department of Education
proposals: Abolish the Department of Education and return control to states
Move IDEA to HHS, NCES to the Census Bureau; move Title I to HHS and phase it out
Move the Office for Civil Rights to DOJ, limited to litigation; drop pending Title IX gender-identity investigations
Restore the 2020 Title IX rule and define 'sex' as biological; require guardian consent for pronoun use
Oppose student-loan forgiveness; expand vouchers usable at private and religious schools

chapters.title: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
proposals: Eliminate the Loan Programs Office, the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations and the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
Repeal the Inflation Reduction Act's energy provisions; curtail the Grid Deployment Office
Redirect national-laboratory funding away from climate and renewables
'No industrial policy nor economy-wide climate policy' (chapter wording per OnTheIssues excerpt)
Eliminate or overhaul the Office of State and Community Energy Programs

chapters.title: Environmental Protection Agency
proposals: Reverse the 2009 greenhouse-gas endangerment finding and end federal GHG regulation
Close the Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights; downsize the agency
Bar states (California) from setting stricter vehicle-emission rules
Revisit PFAS hazardous-substance designations (per CNN's mapping)
Reorient science advisory bodies (CPR notes dismissal of the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee as matching the chapter)

chapters.title: Department of Health and Human Services
proposals: Reverse FDA approval of mifepristone (CNN's mapping) and enforce the Comstock Act (18 U.S.C. 1461/1462) against mailed abortion pills
End mandatory insurance coverage of Ella ('potential abortifacient'); defund Planned Parenthood; require states to report abortion data to CDC as a Medicaid condition
Medicaid work requirements, time limits or lifetime caps; promote Medicare Advantage
Eliminate Head Start; direct child-care funding to at-home care
Deny gender-affirming care at federal providers; restore the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division; make NIH staff easier to fire and remove DEI

chapters.title: Department of Housing and Urban Development
proposals: Repeal the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing rule (p. 509) and end Property Appraisal and Valuation Equity policies
End Housing First; add work requirements and time limits for rental assistance
Bar noncitizens including mixed-status families from federally assisted housing
Raise FHA premiums on mortgages over 20 years; limit FHA to first-time buyers
Congress to consider a 'wholesale overhaul' devolving HUD functions to states and localities; convert career leadership posts to political ones

chapters.title: Department of the Interior
proposals: Expand onshore and offshore oil and gas lease sales; open the Arctic Coastal Plain and most of the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska; expand Willow
Restart federal coal leasing; approve the Ambler Road
Seek repeal of the Antiquities Act; shrink national monuments; end the 30x30 conservation initiative
Delist grizzly bears and gray wolves; reinstate Trump-era limits on the ESA and the Migratory Bird Treaty Act
Relocate BLM headquarters west; restore Trump-era NEPA limits

chapters.title: Department of Justice
proposals: 'Top-to-bottom overhaul' of DOJ and FBI; FBI director personally accountable to the president; expand political appointees
Review all major FBI investigations and end those deemed unlawful or contrary to the national interest
Have the Civil Rights Division sue employers and institutions over DEI and affirmative-action programs; curtail police consent decrees
Take legal action against local district attorneys who decline to prosecute
Enforce 18 U.S.C. 1461/1462 (Comstock) against mailed abortion pills; expand the federal death penalty

chapters.title: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
proposals: Eliminate DEI programs and federal funding for critical-race-theory training; end race/ethnicity data collection in employment
Eliminate disparate-impact liability; remove sexual-orientation and gender-identity protections
Require premium pay for Sunday/Sabbath work (needs Congress); exempt small businesses from OSHA fines
Allow teenage workers in currently prohibited hazardous jobs (CCA cites p. 627)
Cap and phase down H-2A and H-2B visas; shrink the NLRB (Wikipedia)

chapters.title: Department of Transportation
proposals: Replace discretionary grants with block grants
Reduce fuel-economy (CAFE) requirements
Stop federal funding of bike lanes, sidewalks and trails; reject 'Vision Zero'
Reduce public-transit funding and rail-safety regulation
Encourage airline consolidation; reduce pilot flight-hour requirements

chapters.title: Department of Veterans Affairs
proposals: Rescind VA coverage of abortion services and gender-reassignment surgery
Privatize disability medical examinations; shift from full-time employees to contractors
End the Office of Accountability and Whistleblower Protection
Recruit retired physicians; cut VA funding (Wikipedia's summary)

chapters.title: Department of Commerce
proposals: Break up and downsize NOAA; privatize the National Weather Service; eliminate marine sanctuaries
Abolish the Economic Development Administration
Add a citizenship question to the census; merge BEA, Census and BLS
Place TikTok and WeChat on the Entity List
Abolish advisory committees not required by statute

chapters.title: Department of the Treasury
proposals: Two-rate income tax (15%/30%); corporate rate 18%; top capital-gains rate 15%; three-fifths vote to raise taxes
Repeal the Corporate Transparency Act
Withdraw from the Paris Agreement and UNFCCC, the OECD, the World Bank and the IMF
Privatize Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; repeal much of Dodd-Frank (FSOC, disclosure rules)
Reverse ESG support; eliminate the U.S. Trade and Development Agency

chapters.title: Export-Import Bank
authors: Veronique de Rugy ('The Export-Import Bank Should Be Abolished')
Jennifer Hazelton ('The Case for the Export-Import Bank')
proposals: Debate chapter: de Rugy argues to abolish the Export-Import Bank; Hazelton argues to retain it

chapters.title: Federal Reserve
proposals: Gradually abolish the Fed and back the dollar with a commodity such as gold (Wikipedia's summary)
Remove full employment from the Fed's mandate
Merge Fed supervision with OCC, FDIC and NCUA
Ban a US central bank digital currency in favor of private dollar-backed stablecoins

chapters.title: Small Business Administration
proposals: Allow SBA loans to religious entities
Reduce SBA disaster-relief lending

chapters.title: Trade
authors: Peter Navarro ('The Case for Fair Trade')
Kent Lassman ('The Case for Free Trade')
proposals: Navarro: reciprocal, higher tariffs on the EU, China and India; restrict US investment in sensitive Chinese sectors
Lassman: lower or eliminate tariffs and pursue more free-trade agreements

chapters.title: Financial Regulatory Agencies
authors: David R. Burton (Securities and Exchange Commission and Related Agencies)
proposals: Abolish the CFPB (reverse Dodd-Frank Sec. 1061); if courts strike its funding, order immediate dissolution; repeal Sec. 1071 small-business lending data rule
Abolish FINRA and the PCAOB (CCA summary)
Investigate corporate ESG as cover for unfair or anticompetitive practices

chapters.title: Federal Communications Commission
proposals: Ban TikTok (described as a national-security imperative)
Require social-media platforms not to remove mainstream political positions; impose Big Tech transparency obligations
Allow more media consolidation
Consider revoking NPR stations' noncommercial status (Wikipedia's summary)

chapters.title: Federal Election Commission
proposals: Stop the FEC from countering 'misinformation' about election integrity (Wikipedia's summary)
Excerpt per OnTheIssues: treating correction ('curing') of mail-in ballots as voter fraud

chapters.title: Federal Trade Commission
proposals: Create an ESG/DEI 'collusion' task force targeting firms (especially private equity) using ESG to fix prices or reduce output
Treat platforms' advertising to and contracting with children as potentially deceptive; consider written parental consent
Coordinate with state attorneys general on Big Tech, hospital and supermarket mergers
Recalibrate antitrust and consumer-protection enforcement (Wikipedia separately lists 'abolish the FTC' among project proposals)

trackers.name: Project 2025 Tracker (project2025.observer) - Adrienne Cobb (r/Keep_Track) and u/mollynaquafina
trackers.figure: 55% overall (completed count in full, in-progress count half); 141 completed, 70 in progress, 110 not started of 321 objectives across 34 agencies; most recent completion Aug 12, 2026 (Treasury: repeal of the Corporate Transparency Act)
trackers.note: Fetched directly. Per-agency: USAID 100% (6), CPB 100%, NIH 100%, White House 92% (13), State 82% (11: 8 done/2 in progress/1 not started), Interior 73% (15: 10/2/3), Treasury 43% (15: 5/3/7). Timeline shows only one completion per month through most of 2026 (Jan 15, Jan 22, Feb 12, Mar 1, Apr 24, May 1, Jun 30, Jul 10, Jul 22, Aug 12). Origins: Feb 5, 2025 Keep_Track Substack spreadsheet 'nearly 300' objectives, 70 implemented (https://keeptrack.substack.com/p/project-2025-tracker-is-now-live); Fast Company Feb 28, 2025: 36% (https://www.fastcompany.com/91286705/project-2025-tracker-website-trump-second-term).

trackers.name: Project 2025 Tracker (project2025.observer) - historical readings
trackers.figure: Apr 28, 2025: 97 of 312 (Ms.); Aug 5, 2025: 115 of 317 (46%), 63 in progress (Independent); Oct 13, 2025: 48%, 119 done/66 in progress (Newsweek); Oct 27, 2025: 318 objectives, pace fell from 13/month (Jan-Jul) to ~1/month (Newsweek 'stalled'); Dec 22, 2025: 50%, 126 done/67 in progress of 319 (Newsweek); Aug 23, 2026: 141/70/110 of 321 (Baller Alert)
trackers.note: Sources: https://msmagazine.com/2025/04/28/trump-project-2025-plan-reproductive-rights-abortion-lgbtq-childcare-title-ix/ ; https://www.aol.com/trump-nearly-halfway-project-2025-190141640.html ; https://www.newsweek.com/project-2025-trump-has-implemented-half-of-conservative-plan-tracker-10874076 ; https://www.newsweek.com/project-2025-has-stalled-tracker-10932443 ; https://balleralert.com/project-2025-progress-completed-in-progress-pending-2026/ . Cobb to The Cut (via Newsweek): 'I don't think the absence of progress on these goals can be interpreted as an unwillingness to complete them.'

trackers.name: Center for Progressive Reform + Governing for Impact 'Project 2025 Tracker' (domestic regulatory agenda, 20 agencies, 532 recommended executive actions)
trackers.figure: 53%: 283 of 532 recommended actions initiated or completed in the first 12 months
trackers.note: Earlier readings: 28% (May 5, 2025, https://progressivereform.org/cpr-blog/project-2025-at-100-days-part-i/); 47%, 251 of 532 completed, 'almost 1 action per day' (Oct 15, 2025, https://progressivereform.org/publications/tracking-project-2025-update-oct2025). Note: this is the Center for Progressive Reform, not the Center for American Progress; no standalone Center for American Progress tracker was found in this session.

trackers.name: Reproductive Freedom for All - 'Tracking Project 2025' (reproductive-health actions)
trackers.figure: 57 actions tracked; 24 completed, 10 in progress; '58% completed or in progress'; page also states 55% of Project 2025 overall implemented
trackers.note: Page last modified Oct 27, 2026. The 19th/PBS (Dec 24, 2025) cited RFA at ~40% of reproductive-rights policies implemented as of Nov 2025 (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/amp/politics/tracking-how-much-of-project-2025-the-trump-administration-achieved-this-year).

trackers.name: Heritage Foundation's own claim (fundraising email)
trackers.figure: 53% of Project 2025 proposals implemented, per Heritage fundraising email
trackers.note: Bloomberg Law (Ian Kullgren). Email credited gutting USAID and stripping DEI; urged supporters to 'implement all of Heritage's policy recommendations' in 'this special 250th anniversary year.' Heritage spokespeople did not respond. Heritage's April 2023 press release claimed Trump 'embraced nearly 64% of the 2016 edition's policy solutions after one year' (via FactCheck.org Sept 29, 2025).

trackers.name: TIME analysis of first-week executive actions
trackers.figure: 'Nearly two-thirds' of executive actions issued so far mirror or partially mirror Project 2025 proposals
trackers.note: Nik Popli. Examples: National Guard to border, refugee suspension, Alaska drilling, Paris withdrawal, Schedule F revival, hiring freeze, transgender military ban, WHO withdrawal. Heritage declined to comment.

trackers.name: CNN review of first-week actions
trackers.figure: 36 of 53 first-week executive orders/actions evoke Mandate for Leadership proposals; first EO revoked 67 Biden orders of which at least 15 were singled out by the Mandate
trackers.note: Steve Contorno and Casey Tolan. Divergences noted: TikTok ban paused; Trump 'very unlikely' to restrict mifepristone. Dans: 'This is exactly the work we set out to do.' White House (Harrison Fields): Trump 'had nothing to do with Project 2025.'

trackers.name: BBC (via Yahoo) one-year assessment
trackers.figure: Cites CPR 53% and 'a separate Project 2025 tracker' at 51%
trackers.note: Article references a State of the Union 'Tuesday evening' and Maduro's removal 'earlier this year'; exact date not shown. Heritage statement to BBC: 'all policy and personnel decisions are up to President Trump and his team.' Dans: Project 2025 is 'conservative gospel right now.'

trackers.name: NPR one-year report
trackers.note: Dans: 'I believe the proof is in the pudding'; 'Every day that President Trump rolls out another Project 2025 item, it's really an endorsement of our work.' Lists implemented: immigration crackdown, dismantling Education Dept, ending DEI, workforce overhaul, funding freeze (partly blocked), two-genders policy.

trackers.name: FactCheck.org implementation series
trackers.figure: Item-by-item status (no percentage): workforce cuts >200,000 (done); union rights ended at 40 agencies (done); Schedule F (partial, stayed); impoundment (largely blocked); CPB defunded $1.1B (done); Education Dept staff halved (partial); CFPB 1,500 to 200 staff (partial); FEMA elimination (not done)
trackers.note: Eugene Kiely. Dans quoted: efforts 'exceeded my expectations. My wildest dreams, if you will.'

hearing.title: Kitchen Table Economics: How Failed Biden-Harris Policies Continue to Hurt Consumers
hearing.committee: House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs (10:00 am, 2154 Rayburn)
witnesses: Paul Winfree, Ph.D., President & CEO, Economic Policy Innovation Center (author of Project 2025 Ch. 24, Federal Reserve)
Patrice Onwuka, Director, Center for Economic Opportunity, Independent Women's Forum
Chuck DeVore, Chief National Initiatives Officer, Texas Public Policy Foundation
Brendan Duke (minority witness), Senior Director, Economic Policy, Center for American Progress
hearing.note: The congress.gov file HHRG-118-GO05-20240925-SD004.pdf is a supplementary document from this meeting (GO05 = this subcommittee; meeting ID 117694). Oversight Democrats' release says Rep. Melanie Stansbury (Vice Ranking Member) noted Winfree wrote a Project 2025 chapter and entered the Mandate into the hearing record: 'It is the playbook that was put forward by the conservative community for the next administration' (https://oversightdemocrats.house.gov/news/press-releases/subcommittee-hearing-oversight-democrats-champion-biden-harris-administrations). The congress.gov PDF itself could not be fetched, so its identity as the Mandate text is inferred. Same day, the House Judiciary Select Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government also discussed Project 2025 (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-118hhrg56926/html/CHRG-118hhrg56926.htm). The prior day's full-committee Oversight hearing (Sept 24, 2024, meeting 117685) entered a CNN review of Project 2025 contributors as SD019 (https://docs.house.gov/meetings/GO/GO00/20240924/117685/HHRG-118-GO00-20240924-SD019.pdf).

distancing.quote: Despite our being crystal clear, some 'allies' haven't gotten the hint. (Susie Wiles and Chris LaCivita campaign statement; month per Axios)

I know nothing about Project 2025. I have no idea who is behind it. I disagree with some of the things they're saying and some of the things they're saying are absolutely ridiculous and abysmal. Anything they do, I wish them luck, but I have nothing to do with them. (Truth Social)
Trump at a July 2024 rally called the plan 'seriously extreme,' conceived by people on the 'severe right' (Axios paraphrase)
I have nothing to do with Project 2025. That's out there. I haven't read it. I don't want to read it, purposely. I'm not going to read it. (presidential debate with Kamala Harris)
Trump 'had nothing to do with Project 2025.' (White House spokesman Harrison Fields to CNN)

I have a meeting today with Russ Vought, he of PROJECT 2025 Fame, to determine which of the many Democrat Agencies... I can't believe the Radical Left Democrats gave me this unprecedented opportunity. (Truth Social; first public embrace, during the shutdown)

boasts.quote: we are in the process of the second American Revolution, which will remain bloodless if the left allows it to be (Bannon's War Room; prompted Trump's July 5 disavowal)
Honestly, I'm ecstatic... this is exceeding our expectations and our expectations were high (Steve Gruber Show, on cabinet picks)
It is fair and there's no doubt that that will happen (UnHerd, asked whether the Project 2025 agenda will be implemented)
This is exactly the work we set out to do. (to CNN)
It's actually way beyond my wildest dreams... The deep state is going to get its breath back. (to Politico's Michael Hirsh, ~two-month mark)
Americans 'should be taking a victory lap'; credited Trump with starting 'the dismantling of the administrative state'; called mass deportations 'glorious' (NPR All Things Considered)
exceeded my expectations. My wildest dreams, if you will. (quoted by FactCheck.org)
I believe the proof is in the pudding... Every day that President Trump rolls out another Project 2025 item, it's really an endorsement of our work. (NPR)
Project 2025 'really change the game in terms of closing the door on the progressive era' (PBS/AP, on ending Senate bid)
53% of Project 2025 implemented; 'That is a big deal' (Bloomberg Law)

history.what: The Heritage Foundation publishes Mandate for Leadership: The Conservative Promise, the 900-page Project 2025 policy book, 30 chapters by some 400 contributors
Trump on Truth Social: “I know nothing about Project 2025. I have no idea who is behind it.”
Paul Dans, Project 2025’s director, leaves Heritage as the campaign distances itself from the project
House Oversight subcommittee hearing with Paul Winfree (Ch. 24 author) as a witness; Democrats enter the Mandate into the record
Inauguration; the first executive orders, two-thirds of which mirror Mandate proposals by Time’s count
Trump on Truth Social: a meeting with “Russ Vought, he of PROJECT 2025 Fame” — the first public embrace
